newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliament rejects wealth tax cap.
newsitem.headline: French parliament rejects wealth tax cap.

text.p: The French parliament on Tuesday killed a plan to limit a wealth tax on the very rich despite initial backing for the idea from President Jacques Chirac and the ruling centre-right coalition.
A committee of members of the Senate and National Assembly, set up to reconcile differences between their two versions of the 1997 finance bill, voted by eight to five to drop the wealth tax cap.
Some deputies from Chirac's Gaullist RPR party voted with the Socialist and Communist opposition to kill the proposal.

The measure, limiting the amount payable in wealth tax to 80 percent of annual income, would have benefited France's 1,000 richest taxpayers. The government said they should be encouraged to stay in France rather than flee to avoid taxes.

Jubilant opposition Socialist spokesman Claude Bartolone said even government supporters had finally realised they could not lead France out of economic stagnation by giving more to the "haves" and taking more from the "have nots".
Gaullist floor-leader Michel Pericard expressed relief that "a wise decision has avoided a somewhat ridiculous confrontation between the Senate and the Assembly".
The ruling coalition had initially backed the move in a drive to prevent capital flight but denounced by the opposition as a gift to the ultra-rich.

Chirac and Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure argued that a ceiling on wealth tax, abolished last year, should be restored, saying the change had driven top millionaires to live abroad for tax purposes, costing France investment and jobs.
But backbenchers successfully argued it would be a political liability in times of austerity.

Among those who voted to kill the tax cap were Gaullist Jean-Francois Coppe, a close supporter of Prime Minister Alain Juppe, suggesting the government may have concluded the measure would have been more trouble than it was worth.
Centrist deputy Pierre Mehaignerie, who favoured the cap but did not vote on Tuesday, urged the government to submit a new proposal to achieve the same goal.
